newsitem.title: USA: CanOxy sees 97 earns down C$20M, output up 5.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy sees 97 earns down C$20M, output up 5.7 pct.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd said it saw earnings in 1997 down by C$20 million at around $170 million.

Investment relations director Kevin Finn, speaking at FirstEnergy Capital's East Coast Canadian Energy Conference in New York, declined to comment on the company's first quarter earnings but said he expected all of 1997 to be lower due mainly to higher exploration costs.
Finn also forecast a 5.7 percent increase in oil and gas production in 1997 due to growth in western Canada and the U.S. Gulf Coast.
The 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) of oil equivelant rise will boost production from 175,000 bpd of oil equivalent (boe) in 1996 to 185,000 in 1997, said Finn.
"We expect Western Canada to grow substantially," he said. "Crude production will increase from 14,000 barrels per day to 17,500."
The company's gas production in the U.S. Gulf Coast -- particularly off Louisiana -- will also increase, from 80 million cubic feet per day in 1996 to 115 mmccf in 1997, said Finn.
On Thursday, the company announced new exploration concessions in Indonesia, including a 10 percent interest in the 1.66 million acre Maratua Block.
Exploration costs will also funnel into concessions in Yemen, the U.S. and Canada, the company said.
